 Order

This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 06.08.2019 passed by learned II Additional Member MACT, Khargone in Claim Case No.100170/2016 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Shaharyan @ Jishant the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.17,05,311/- along with interest from the date of filing of claim petition till realization.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The claimants have filed salary certificate of the deceased Ex.A-247 Hence, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Learned counsel for the claimants submitted that deceased was working as Assistant under the Chartered Accountant and received a salary of Rs.7,000/- as per salary certificate Ex.A-247.
6.

The claimants examined Sachin Mahajan Chartered Accountant who stated that the deceased was working with him as a computer operator and he gave Rs.7,000/- per month, but he accepted in cross examination that he has not produced any document to show that deceased was regularly present in his office and he has not mentioned in his income tax return that he paid Rs.7,000/- to the deceased.
In the cross examination he also stated that deceased was working with him and did travelling work.
The accident took in December, 2014.
So this pay certificate is of no benefit to the claimants.
7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

Considering the evidence that came on record,

2 in the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal for calculating the compensation amount is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced to Rs.5,000/-.
8.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments made b y the counsel for the appellant and the evidence that came on record, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Loss of dependency (Income of Rs.5,000/- plus Rs.2,000/-(40%FP) = deceased)
Rs.7,000/- less 1/2 =Rs.3,500/- x 12 x 18 = Rs.7,56,000/-
 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 Consortium Rs.80,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.9,58,911/-

Total Amount Rs.18,24,911/-
9.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case i s Rs.18,24,911/-as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.17,05,311/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.1,19,600/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
10. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.

The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact (HIRDESH) JUDGE RJ Mohammad Rafiq vs Ritesh on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46827219/
